title: Akshar Yoga Kendraa Sets 21 Guinness World Records on International Yoga Day
excerpt: Over 10,000 participants from more than 100 countries gathered in Bengaluru for what became one of the largest coordinated yoga record attempts in history.
body:
• Akshar Yoga Kendraa set 21 Guinness World Records on International Yoga Day 2026 in Bengaluru, India
  • Over 10,000 participants from 100+ countries took part, including military personnel, NCC cadets, and specially-abled individuals
  • Records spanned 20 different yoga asanas and one mass Tratak meditation with 7,000 participants
  • The event was led by Himalayan Siddhaa Akshar and verified by two Guinness World Records adjudicators

A Day of 21 Records

Bengaluru became the global capital of yoga on International Yoga Day 2026, as Akshar Yoga Kendraa set 21 Guinness World Records in a single day — one of the largest coordinated yoga record attempts ever conducted, according to Guinness World Records.

Led by yoga master Himalayan Siddhaa Akshar, the event drew over 10,000 participants from more than 100 countries, including the United States, United Kingdom, Italy, Taiwan, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Singapore, and the UAE.

Two Guinness World Records adjudicators — Mbali Nkosi and Swapnil Dangarikar — were on site to verify the results. All 20 asana record attempts succeeded on the first try.

The Records

The session began with mass Tratak meditation by 7,000 participants, followed by 20 simultaneous yoga pose attempts. Among the records set, according to Guinness World Records' official account:

The most people performing the chair pose simultaneously: 1,695. The most people performing the bridge pose simultaneously: 1,692. The most people performing a Warrior II pose simultaneously: 1,634. The most people performing a shoulder stand simultaneously: 1,633.

Other records included downward facing dog (864 participants), mermaid pose (863), eagle pose (552), butterfly pose (550), Warrior III (529), pistol squat (514), locust pose (539), and double toe hold (461).

"Today is not merely about setting records; it is about awakening human potential. Yoga teaches us that true success comes from discipline, awareness, and inner mastery."

— Himalayan Siddhaa Akshar, Akshar Yoga Kendraa founder

Diverse Participation

The gathering included personnel from the BSF, CISF, CRPF, Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and Karnataka State Police alongside NCC cadets, specially-abled individuals, children from orphanages, corporate leaders, entrepreneurs, and students, according to Media Brief.

Akshar Yoga Kendraa is recognized as an Accreditation Body under the Yoga Institution category by the Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India. The organization had previously set 12 yoga-related Guinness records in April 2026, which Guinness World Records described as reflecting "a clear desire to make sure yoga can benefit as many people as possible."

India's Yoga Diplomacy

The mass record attempt comes as India continues to leverage yoga as a soft-power tool globally. Separately, the Ministry of AYUSH organized a nationwide yoga session on June 14 as part of the Yoga Day countdown, drawing 435,831 participants across the country in its own Guinness record attempt.

For the Indian diaspora, yoga remains one of the strongest cultural connectors to the homeland. Events like the Akshar Yoga Kendraa records reinforce India's position as the world's premier yoga destination and training hub, with growing numbers of international students traveling to cities like Bengaluru, Rishikesh, and Mysuru for certified instruction.
nri_angle: Yoga remains one of the strongest cultural connectors for the Indian diaspora, with record events reinforcing India's global yoga leadership.
